items.title: Slide Hampton interviewed by Monk Rowe, West Orange, New Jersey, July 30, 2003
items.q: There was ... Jack Teagarden ... So we were listening to all of them and actually we wasn’t really thinking about having a favorite. We were just loving all of it and learning, enjoying listening and learning from all of them.

ctx.x: Sure. Who were the influences on the trombone for you back then?

There were many. At that time there were many trombone players that were very popular. Later in the fifties and sixties you started not to hear much of trombone players anymore. But in the forties and fifties there were a lot of trombone players that were popular. There was Tommy Dorsey, there was Trummy Young, there finally was J.J. Johnson, there was Jack Teagarden, there was Lawrence Brown. A thousand guys you know. So we were listening to all of them and actually we wasn’t really thinking about having a…
Neat. You were, let’s see, you were born in ’32?
